A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RVM work. Their complete main text and supplementary material are readable, and equations, tables, figures, and relocated appendix content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original RVM benchmark results, controlled ablations, temporal-stability measurements, and qualitative feature analyses in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: V2 retains the original RVM experiments and ablations, revises baseline results, and adds a latency-versus-sequence-length comparison.

M1.justification: The per-frame ViT, transformer-based gated recurrent core, asymmetric masking, reconstruction decoder, and pixel-level L2 objective remain unchanged. The architectural equations and supplementary pseudocode are also retained.

E1.justification: The training mixture and eight downstream benchmarks remain the same, including the supplementary MOVI-E training setup for point tracking. Long-sequence DAVIS and synthetic moving-noise examples are retained. The added latency analysis does not establish a new data domain or task.

E2.justification: The principal comparisons are substantially revised: Table 2 adds distilled DINOv2-S, while distilled 4DS-B disappears from both the tabulated comparison and Figure 1. Table 1 reports V-JEPA2-L/H instead of V-JEPA-L/H, although unchanged Appendix 12.2 leaves the actual checkpoint change unclear. SiamMAE-B, ordinary 4DS-B, and VideoMAE-B remain in appendix Table 10.

E3.justification: New Appendix Section 13 evaluates inference latency in seconds against sequence length, plotted up to 1,000 frames. Existing training schedules, readout protocols, label-propagation settings, and ablation controls are unchanged. Hardware, batch size, and other timing conditions are not specified for the new comparison.

E4.justification: Figure 8 adds a computational-scaling analysis comparing RVM, DINOv2, VideoMAE, and V-JEPA2 as frame count increases. The source-frame, temporal-aggregator, and training-volume ablations remain unchanged, as do the temporal-stability and qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results and latency plot do not introduce uncertainty estimation or error bars.

E6.justification: Baseline evidence in the central tables changes substantially. SiamMAE-S SSv2 changes from 56.0 to 40.0, ScanNet AbsRel from 1.00 to 1.63, and a previously missing Kinetics score becomes 41.2. The newly labeled V-JEPA2 rows have revised scores, rather than establishing same-model performance changes. V2 also adds DINOv2-S results, Table 2 normalized averages, and latency curves, while removing distilled 4DS-B results. RVM scores and ablation values are unchanged; base-scale results are relocated.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, masking formulation, recurrent update equations, and architectural reasoning are unchanged. The new latency plot supports an existing scaling argument without introducing a theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract sharpens the spatial-performance claim from performing favorably against image models to matching or exceeding them. The central claims about generalist representations, small models without distillation, up to 30-fold parameter efficiency, and stable long-horizon processing remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.2 now explicitly acknowledges that distilled DINOv2-S beats RVM-S on three benchmarks, qualifying the small-model comparison. New Appendix Section 14 notes the modest improvement from RVM-S to RVM-B, and the latency discussion strengthens the streaming interpretation. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Training-data recipes, architecture tables, pseudocode, hardware and precision information, evaluation hyperparameters, and access links are retained. V2 does not supply additional checkpoint documentation for its revised comparisons or implementation details for the latency analysis.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work section remain essentially unchanged. Positioning is modestly refined: v2 removes the broad claim that omitting patch normalization differs from prior work, drops the characterization of 4DS as requiring distillation, and shifts the main experimental discussion to the already-cited V-JEPA2.

P1.justification: The abstract, parts of the introduction, and small-model discussion are rewritten. Terminology shifts from video tasks to spatio-temporal tasks, two short appendix sections are added, and acknowledgments are edited. The overall narrative and most technical prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Table 1 is reordered and restyled, and Table 2 gains an average column while its base-scale rows move to new Table 10. A latency figure is added. Several existing figures are relocated or renumbered, but their qualitative imagery and the temporal-stability plot are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a useful small-model comparator, acknowledges DINOv2-S advantages, and supplies a latency plot. However, it removes the distilled 4DS-B comparison and introduces unresolved consistency problems: Section 4.2.2 retains the old +3.7% SSv2 claim after the corresponding SiamMAE-S score changes, while Table 1 reports V-JEPA2 but Appendix 12.2 still describes V-JEPA. The latency plot also lacks timing conditions. These benefits and losses do not establish a reliable net improvement.
